- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates downward trends in sentiment-heavy negative periods — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +1.2, -1.4, +0.3), model tends to lag in adjusting to sentiment shifts — delay forecast correction by 1–2 days if sentiment changes direction.
- Model often ignores sentiment volatility — if sentiment swings >1.0 in 3 consecutive days, adjust forecast to reflect higher uncertainty (add ±0.5–1.0 to forecast range).
